project_overview: This project appears to be a complex web application likely managing student data, admissions, and exam results. The architecture utilizes a layered approach with distinct components for user interfaces, data handling, and potentially backend services.  The presence of numerous Vue components suggests a component-driven development style.  The extensive use of `router` and specific routes indicates a single-page application (SPA) structure.

layers.description: Contains the core application logic and rules.

macro_trends.title: Low-Level Component Import Issues
macro_trends.description: Several Vue components (e.g., ExamFormSubmission, ResultPage) are importing utilities potentially related to UI or UI/UX elements. This can introduce fragility as changes to low-level components may unexpectedly impact higher-level components. It’s a prime area for cross-layer contamination.

macro_trends.title: Potential State Management Fragility
macro_trends.description: The large number of Vue components suggests a potential for complex state management. Deep prop-drilling or inconsistent state patterns could lead to difficult-to-debug issues and reduced maintainability.

key_workflows.name: Student Enrollment & Admission
key_workflows.description: This workflow likely involves user registration, course selection, application submission, and ultimately, admission processing.  The involved components (e.g., `iLikeCourses`, `ExamFormSubmission`, `SelectedApplicationService`) suggest a process of selecting courses and potentially taking exams as part of the admissions criteria.

key_workflows.name: Exam Result Processing
key_workflows.description: This workflow encompasses the submission of exam results, the generation of marksheets, and the display of student performance.  Components like `ExamFormSubmission`, `ResultPage`, and `viewMarksheet` are central to this process, indicating a critical pathway with potential for errors impacting student assessment.
